These choices live only on this device and are kept as soon as you change them. Nothing here is sent to DailyGammon.
Change Password and Public Profile stay on the site; this app never sends them.
Deco: black enamel, gold and small gears
Deco: ivory, brass and small gears

The dice, the checkers and the doubling cube knock on wood, in any theme. With Show which point I\'m pressing on, a tap on a point you can\'t move from gives a double knock. Silent mode on the device and TalkBack keep them quiet.
Each match gets its own board from the ticked ones above and keeps it every time you open it. Turn this off and the board you chose comes back.
One die for each move, played ones greyed
Two dice, as on the site, played ones greyed
Points won, as on the site
Spinning arc in the board\'s colours
Ouroboros, a snake chasing its tail
Hourglass, sand falling and turning over
Golden laurel wreath growing leaf by leaf
Golden laurel wreath with a gleam running along it
The same shape in black enamel and gold with small gears. It has colours of its own and does not follow the board.

When a checker has only one legal play in every possible turn (coming in from the bar, bearing off, doubles), the app places it before you start. You still choose the rest and press Submit Move yourself. Undo Move clears these as well.

While you build a move, each step is drawn as an arrow from where the checker left to where it landed, until you press Submit Move. Doubles show as a chain, and checkers the app placed for you get arrows too. Arrows appear only when the app composes the move itself, not when the board follows the site\'s own links.
Show arrows for the opponent\'s move

On your turn, the opponent\'s last move is drawn as arrows in their colour next to their dice, until you roll. The move is read from the match\'s Review Game page, so each board you open on your turn asks DailyGammon for one more page.

While your finger is on the board, the number of the point under it grows at the board edge, where the finger doesn\'t cover it. Orange means a checker can move from there, crossed out on a dark tile means it can\'t. The number stays for a moment after you lift your finger, so a quick tap shows where it landed.
Submit the move by tapping the dice

When your turn is complete and the dice have gone grey, tapping them sends the move, exactly as Submit Move does. A turn where only one die can be played counts as complete, so tapping sends it too. There is no confirmation, the same as the button.
Swap the dice by tapping them

Before you pick up the first checker, while no die has gone grey, tapping the dice swaps their order the way Swap Dice does. Nothing is sent to DailyGammon, and tapping again swaps back. Doubles cannot be swapped.

With this on, the match list, messages, forum and settings stay portrait; turn it off if you hold the tablet sideways and do not want it to rotate when you return to the match list. The board has its own switch below. On a phone every screen turns upright while you type, so the field and its button stay above the keyboard, and the sign-in screen is always upright. On a tablet with Android 16 or later, Android turns every screen with the device, so neither this switch nor the board\'s has any effect there.
Turn the board with the device

With this off, the board is always landscape, where the checkers are largest. With this on, the board follows the way you hold the device, and upright it fills the width of the screen with the side panel below it. On a phone the checkers are then smaller. While you write a message, a reminder or a mark, the board turns upright either way so the keyboard has room.
Hide the status and navigation bars

With this on, the bars are hidden on every screen. Swipe inwards from the edge of the screen to bring them into view for a moment, with Back on them. With this off, they are hidden only on the board, and only when they would make the board smaller.

The side panel goes to your other hand, so one hand moves checkers while the other reaches the buttons. Right-handed keeps the panel on the left, which is the default. With the board upright the panel is below it, so this has no effect there. The two pictures are mirror images: Left hand shows the home board on the left, on the side of the hand that moves the checkers. The board turns that way when Home boards on left side is ticked under DailyGammon at the top of this screen.
No folder chosen. Pick a folder on this device, and its pictures fill the room left below the lists.
Pictures come from %1$s on this device.

Pictures are shown whole, never cropped: one, two or three at a time depending on how much room is left, and every screen you open picks new ones. Text stays on its plain surface, and the board never shows them.
Colour names by rating, tournaments by rounds and the Inbox count by size

A player\'s name takes a colour by the rating this device has seen: grey below 1600, green from 1600, blue from 1800, purple from 2000 and orange from 2200. The Inbox message count uses the same colours. A tournament\'s name takes them by its number of rounds, that is the matches in a row it takes to win: grey up to 4, green 5, blue 6, purple 7 or 8 and orange from 9, and a Champs or yearly tournament is always orange. Turn it off for plain names everywhere.
Ask for fingerprint or PIN when the app starts

Your message history exists only on this device, and this keeps it closed if someone else has your unlocked device in hand. Any unlock this device offers works: fingerprint, face, PIN, pattern or password. It takes effect the next time the app starts.
This device has no fingerprint, face, PIN, pattern or password set up, so the app would have nothing to unlock with. Set one up in the device settings to use this.

Save to file writes the choices on this page to a file as one line of text, together with the match list order and the Inbox player filter. Keep it wherever you choose, Google Drive included. On the other device, open this page and tap Open file. Your sign-in, app lock, messages, quick messages and pictures folder stay on this device.
The file could not be written. Nothing was saved.
This is not a settings text from DG Android, or part of it is missing. Nothing was changed.
This device already uses these settings. Nothing would change.

Asks once more before Beaver! or Accept Beaver is sent. DailyGammon has no confirmation setting for these, while Accept and Decline follow your DailyGammon settings. Until you change it, it follows Confirmation on offering doubles there.

Once there is no contact, the app places the play that bears off the most checkers. If several plays bear off equally many, it places only what they have in common and leaves the choice to you. Submit Move stays yours.
This is a read-only view. The app does not write anything to DailyGammon, so change these on the site itself.

Nothing here is sent until you press Update Preferences. DailyGammon saves this form as a whole, so every field is sent even if you change one. The app reads the page again before and after sending, and only a matching read-back counts as saved.
This app can\'t show the Mini board.
Changes the page colour on the DailyGammon website only. This app keeps its own background.
This one changes what the "Play!" queue hands out, and that queue is what the message archive reads from.

Forget your credentials on this device; your stored messages stay
What does this app do with my DailyGammon account?

This app signs in to dailygammon.com with your own DailyGammon account. It shows you the same pages the site shows in a browser: your match list, the board, the lounge, the forum and your messages.

DailyGammon has no separate interface for apps. Everything here is read from the site's pages, and everything you do here is the same request a browser would send.

You need a DailyGammon account to start. Accounts are made on dailygammon.com and not in this app. The password comes by email, which can take a while.

What the app adds on top of the site is listed in the next group.
Is my connection to DailyGammon encrypted?

No. dailygammon.com does not offer HTTPS, so everything between this app and the site travels unencrypted: your sign-in, your moves and your messages, both the ones you send and the ones you take.

This is exactly the same risk as playing DailyGammon in a browser. The app can make it neither worse nor better, because encryption would have to come from the site.

Anyone who can watch the network you are on, such as an open Wi-Fi, can read that traffic. Write in a message only what you would write on a postcard.

What the app keeps on this device is a different matter: your password is stored encrypted, and the message archive never leaves the device by itself.
What can I do on the DailyGammon site but not in this app?

A few things stay on the site. Where you would look for them in the app, it tells you so.

Create Account: accounts are made on dailygammon.com, and this app does not open that page.

Change Password and Public Profile: the row above the DailyGammon settings form opens the site's settings page in your browser.

The Mini board: its Board Scheme card can't be chosen, and if Mini is already set on the site, the board screen asks you to choose another scheme there.

Background Color: it is in the settings form, but it changes only the page colour on the website. The app keeps its own background.

Active Game, which steps through a match one position at a time: the app does not show it. Use the site in a browser, or share a finished match as .mat or .sgf and open it in an analysis program.
What is different from the DailyGammon site
Your messages are kept on this device.

DailyGammon shows each message once and keeps no copy of it. Every message you take is saved on this device before it appears on screen.\n\nThe archive is yours alone: it is on this device only, and the developer of this app has no way to see it.
A dropped connection does not sign you out.
The app signs in again quietly when the site asks for it, so a lost connection costs you nothing but the wait.
You can sort the match list your way.
The Sort by buttons order the list by Grace, Time Pool, Round, Length or Opponent. A third tap on the same button brings back the site\'s own order. Your choice is kept on this device.
Your taps stay on this device until you press Submit Move.
Undo Move takes a tap back before anything has left the device. In the browser every click goes to the site at once.
The app can place checkers for you.
Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me only place. The move still leaves this device when you send it, and Undo Move takes their checkers back like any other.
A tournament row names the opponent and the round.

The site\'s tournament page does not say who you are playing. The app fills it in from your match list and from what it last saw of that match.\n\nRefresh on Tournaments also reads the tournament pages where you are waiting for an opponent, and the profiles of opponents whose rating the app has not seen.
You can filter, export, back up and import your archive.

Both sides of the chat and your replies are saved.

The player menu filters the archive to one correspondent. Export writes it to a file, Back up keeps a file current and Import reads such a file back.

These are yours to use. Nobody else, the developer included, can reach your archive.
Each DailyGammon account on this device has its own archive.

If more than one account signs in on this device, each one sees only the messages it took from DailyGammon. Export and Back up write only that account's archive.

Log Out keeps every archive on the device, and they come back when the same account signs in again.

Phrases, reminders and the device settings are shared by all accounts.
Reminders for a game live on this device.

They are notes to yourself, kept until the game ends.\n\nCube reminder is one of them. When you set it, the cube pulses and grows and the robot on it lights its eyes. The cube stays larger with a purple frame until the reminder is gone.
The board can look different from the browser.

Follow my DailyGammon settings matches the browser. The two Monte Carlo looks colour the checkers by your role, not by the site\'s colour.\n\nUntil someone doubles, the cube shows a robot instead of a 1.
Join, Sign Up and forum posts ask you to confirm first. Double and Accept follow your DailyGammon settings.

None of them can be taken back on DailyGammon, so the app asks before it sends. Without your confirmation nothing is sent.

For Double and Accept the choice is yours on DailyGammon. With confirmation off in your settings, the buttons send at once, as they do on the site. Tapping the cube on the board still asks.

In a money game, Confirm Beaver under This device asks before Beaver! and Accept Beaver.
You can mark a position to look at after the match.

Making a mark
Mark position sits next to Reminders on the board. It saves the game score and the move number the site shows, with a comment from you if you want one. Nothing is sent to DailyGammon, and the mark stays on this device until you remove it.

The field is called Comment because that is the word GNU Backgammon, BGBlitz and eXtreme Gammon use for the same thing. Your comment goes into the match file as it is.

The list is on Top Page, under Your turn, grouped by match. When you analyse the match file later, you know which moves to look at first.

Sharing the match file
A finished match on your profile has two buttons. Share .mat hands on the site's own match file. Share .sgf writes the same match for GNU Backgammon, BGBlitz and HedgeHog in GNU Backgammon's format, with your marks as comments and your comment as the comment text.

Share opens the device's share menu. Save to Drive there puts the file in your Google Drive, where Drive for desktop makes it a plain file for the analysis program on your computer.

Nackgammon matches and double repeat matches are not written as .sgf, so share the .mat file for those. Nackgammon starts from its own position, which the export does not write. In double repeat a taken double is played twice for one point each, and the .sgf format has no rule for that. The export reads the tournament page and writes nothing for a double repeat match, even one where nobody doubled.

Where the comment lands
A mark saves the position on the board as well. The export replays the game to find the move that position belongs to, so the comment sits on the move you marked.

A mark made before this, or on a board the app could not read, goes at the start of its game with the site's move number, which is not the game's move number. Step to the position from there.

In the analysis programs
GNU Backgammon shows a comment in its annotation panel, and BGBlitz from version 3.4.5 on its Comment tab. HedgeHog in the browser shows it as a note on the move when you import the file, but on a free account the note did not come back once the match was saved. eXtreme Gammon reads the .sgf but not the comment.

GNU Backgammon also sees a marked move as doubtful, shown as ?! in its move list, so Go › Next marked move (Shift+Ctrl+Page Down) takes you from one mark to the next across the whole match. A mark placed at the start of its game is left without this, so no wrong move is called doubtful.
The board tells you when an action may not have arrived.
If the connection drops while an action is on its way, the board says Nothing was confirmed and never repeats your action by itself. Refresh to see what DailyGammon did.

Top Page is your match list. Your name at the top of Top Page, Lounge and Forum opens your own profile, in the colour your rating has earned.

Lounge shows the site's player list and tournament hall, matches waiting for opponents and tournaments open for sign-up, each behind a heading that folds. Forum is the site's discussion board. These three have Refresh and Settings at the top.

Inbox is your message archive and the place where new items are taken from DailyGammon.

Info holds this text, Connection drops, the site's own Help and Links, the site's Resignation Page and Log Out. The search field at the top of Info finds words in this text and in the site's Help at once. The site's Help is fetched from dailygammon.com for it when you start typing.

Tapping a player's name opens their profile, and a tournament name opens the tournament page, both read from the site. From a profile you can send that player a message. It is saved to your archive because DailyGammon does not keep it.

Another player's profile also shows your record against them, won and lost from your side, read from the site's own Matches versus you page. The row opens those matches.
What do the colours of names and tournaments mean?

Names, tournaments and the Inbox message count take colours like item rarity in a role-playing game: grey, green, blue, purple and orange, from the most common to the rarest.

Players
A player's name takes a colour by rating wherever it appears: on their card beside the board, in the match list, the Lounge, the Forum, profiles, tournament brackets and the Inbox. Grey is below 1600, green from 1600, blue from 1800, purple from 2000 and orange from 2200.

Tournaments
A tournament's name takes a colour by how many matches in a row it takes to win it, which is its number of rounds: grey up to 4, green for 5, blue for 6, purple for 7 or 8 and orange from 9. A Champs tournament is always orange, because only winners of its series get in, and so is a yearly one whose name starts with the year, such as 2026 Open. A tournament that players run among themselves with named private matches has no rounds on the site and stays plain.

Inbox
The count beside a player takes its colour from how that conversation ranks among all your conversations by number of messages. The top 5 % are orange, the next 10 % purple, the next 15 % blue, the next 25 % green and the rest grey. Conversations with the same count share the higher colour, and one message is always grey.

Until the archive has 20 conversations, fixed counts are used instead: green from 2, blue from 5, purple from 10 and orange from 20.

Why so much is grey or plain at first
Grey is where everything starts. DailyGammon gives every new player a rating of 1500, below the 1600 where green begins, and every conversation starts with one message.

A colour also needs something to go on, and a fresh install has seen nothing yet. The app colours a name only after it has seen that player's rating on their profile or in the Lounge player list, and a tournament only after it has seen its rounds in the match list, the Lounge or the tournament page. Until then the name keeps the plain text colour. The board never loads a page just to learn a rating. Refresh on Tournaments is the one place that does, for the opponents in your tournaments, so after it more names have their colours.

Colour names by rating, tournaments by rounds and the Inbox count by size in Settings turns these colours off everywhere.
Why is the match list in this order?

DailyGammon lists your matches in its own order, and that order is a deadline order: the matches nearest to running out of time come first. The app keeps that order until you ask for another one.

The Sort by buttons are Grace, Time Pool, Round, Length and Opponent. Tap one to sort by it, tap it again to reverse, and tap it a third time to return to the order DailyGammon itself uses. An arrow on the button shows the direction.

Your choice is kept on this device, so a button with an arrow means the list is no longer in deadline order.
Does opening a match use up my turn?

No. Opening a match shows the board and does not use up your turn.

The list is reloaded when you come back after playing, since your row has changed. A look without a move leaves it as it was. Answering an invitation in Inbox reloads it as well, since an accepted match joins the list. Coming back to the app from elsewhere while the list is open reloads it too, since time has passed.

Refresh is there when you want it fresh.
Where does a tournament row get the round and the opponent?

Tournaments lists the tournaments you are in. A row with an active game shows the round and the opponent once this device has seen the match. Until then it says opponent's turn, because the Top Page lists only matches where it is your turn. Your wins are shown only when the round is not known, because the round already tells how far you are.

The tournament page itself does not say who the opponent is. The round and the name come from your match list when it is your turn, and otherwise from what the app last saw of that match.

A remembered round can be one behind if the opponent has since finished a game. The line above the list says when the app last saw them, so you can decide whether Refresh is worth pressing.

Refresh on Tournaments reads your tournament list and your profile, so after it every row is current. The first time the list opens on a fresh install, the app reads your profile once by itself.

A row without an active game is waiting for your next opponent, who is still being decided in the other half of the bracket. Refresh reads the tournament page of each such row and adds how many matches there must finish first, for example 2 wins · waiting for 1 match. The number stays until the next Refresh.

Refresh also reads the profile of each opponent whose rating the app has not seen, and the opponent's name takes the same rarity colour by rating as on the board. None of these pages uses up the queue, but they are many, so they are read only when you press Refresh.
How do I move and send a move?

When it is your turn, the board offers the same actions as the site, under the site's own names: Roll Dice, Submit Move, Double and the rest. Tap a point with your checkers to move one from it. The whole column takes the tap, not only the checker.

With Show which point I'm pressing on in Settings, the number of the point under your finger grows at the board edge, where the finger doesn't cover it: orange when a checker can move from there, crossed out on a dark tile when it can't. The number stays for a moment after you lift your finger, so a quick tap shows where it landed. With Game sounds on as well, a tap on a point you can't move from gives a double knock, so you hear a miss without looking.

Your taps are collected on this device and nothing is sent until you press Submit Move. Undo Move takes a tap back before anything has left the device.

With Show arrows for my move on in Settings, each collected step is drawn as an arrow from where the checker left to where it landed, so you can check the move before you send it. Doubles show as a chain, and checkers the app placed for you get arrows too. The arrows go when the move is sent or undone.

With Show arrows for the opponent's move on, the opponent's last move is drawn the same way in their colour when your turn begins, next to their dice. The arrows go when you roll, together with the opponent's dice. The move is read from the match's Review Game page, so each board on your turn asks DailyGammon for one more page. That page is sometimes behind the board, and then no arrows are drawn rather than an older move.

If you turn on Submit the move by tapping the dice in Settings, tapping the dice once the turn is complete sends the move too, exactly as Submit Move does.

When the app cannot verify the position against the page, each tap goes to DailyGammon one at a time instead, exactly as in the browser.
Can the app place checkers for me?

Two settings let the app place checkers for you: Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me.\n\nThey only place. The move still leaves this device when you send it, and Undo Move takes their checkers back like any other.
How do Double and Accept work?

Double and Accept cannot be taken back. When your DailyGammon settings ask for confirmation, they take three steps: tick the site's own Verify box, press the button, then confirm. Without the tick nothing is sent. When your settings ask for none, the site shows no box and the button sends at once.

Tapping the cube is the same action: Double when you can double, Accept when a double is offered to you. It reads the same Verify box, and it always asks you to confirm, even without a box, because a tap on the board is easier to make by accident than a press on a button.

If your DailyGammon settings ask for confirmation on declining doubles, the site shows a Verify Decline box as well. Tick it and press Decline. There is no third step. Each box confirms only its own button, and the app shows exactly the boxes the site shows. On a phone held sideways each box sits on the same row as its button and says just Verify.

In a money game a double offered to you has a third button, Beaver!, and after a beaver your opponent answers with Accept Beaver or Decline. The site has no confirmation setting for these and shows no Verify box for Beaver!.

Confirm Beaver under This device asks once more before either of them sends. Until you change it, it follows Confirmation on offering doubles in your DailyGammon settings.
What does Nothing was confirmed mean?

If the connection drops or the site answers with an error while an action is on its way, the board says so in the middle strip, where the site's own messages go. It gives the reason in a few words (No connection, Site error with its number or Site asleep) followed by Nothing was confirmed. On a crowded board the line sits below the buttons instead.

The position is the last one loaded before the attempt, and nothing on it has been confirmed since. The app never repeats your action by itself. The action buttons are dimmed and do nothing until the board is reloaded.

A Refresh button sits in the middle of the board. Press it to see what DailyGammon did.

When a connection to the site cannot be opened at all, nothing has been sent yet, so the app quietly opens a new one, up to three times, before it shows this.

Each drop is also written to Connection drops on the Info tab: the time, the match, the button and the name of the network error. The list keeps the last hundred, so you can look back after the notice is gone.
How do I refresh the board or go back?

Drag downwards anywhere on the board to load the position again from DailyGammon. The Refresh button does the same.

To leave the board, use Back. When the screen is large enough for the board, the system bar stays on view and Back is always there.

When the bars would cost the board its size, or a bar at the side would narrow the panel, they are hidden. Swipe from the right edge towards the left: it either goes back or brings the bar into view, and Back is on it. You can also swipe downwards from the top edge to bring the status bar into view for a moment.
With Hide the status and navigation bars on in Settings, the bars are hidden on the board and on every other screen, and the same swipes bring them back for a moment.
What is in the panel beside the board?

The panel next to the board carries the site's own links for that match and three things of the app's own.

Layout
With Turn the board with the device on and the device held upright, the board fills the width of the screen and the panel's content moves around it. The match and your opponent are above the board. You, the buttons, Skip Game and the reminders are below it, and each Verify box is to the right of its button.

When the board offers Roll Dice and Double together, the two share one row at equal width, with Verify Double under the left edge of Double. Below them Skip Game shares a row with Mark position, and Reminders with Cube reminder. Handedness has no effect then, because the panel is not beside the board.

Rating colours
The names on the cards take a colour by rating. What the colours mean is under What do the colours of names and tournaments mean?

Chat and reminders
Chat opens a chat box with your opponent above the board, and Reply appears there when the opponent has written. It is not the Send button on a player's profile, which goes to the site's inbox. What you write here goes with your move, because on DailyGammon the message and the move are one and the same step. Both sides of the chat are saved to your archive.

Reminders are notes to yourself for this game, kept on this device until the game ends. Cube reminder is one of them. When you set it, the cube pulses and grows and the robot on it lights its eyes. The cube stays larger with a purple frame until the reminder is gone.

While you write a message, a reminder or a mark, the screen turns upright and the board shrinks so the keyboard has room. Sending, Add, Close or closing the field turns it back.

Skip Game asks DailyGammon for the next waiting item instead of this one. The site hands out each waiting item once, so skipping passes this match by in that queue.\n\nThe match itself is untouched and is still yours to play.
How do I change how the board looks?

Board look in Settings has eight choices.

The eight boards
Follow my DailyGammon settings draws the checkers in the colours the site gives you, so the board matches the browser side by side.

Monte Carlo X-22 draws your checkers cream and always at the bottom, with your opponent in red at the top. Monte Carlo variant is a green felt board with your checkers white and your opponent black. In dark mode its side panel takes the wood of the bearing-off tray instead of black.

Deco is gold and black enamel points on jade felt, with ivory and black checkers ringed in gold.

Maple, Walnut, Oak and leather and Olive are wooden boards: a light maple field in a walnut frame, a dark walnut field with maple and ebony points, an oak frame round a brown leather field, and olive wood with green and red-brown points. The wood has a fine grain. Your checkers are light and your opponent's dark with a light ring. In dark mode the side panel takes the wood of the bearing-off tray.

In the two Monte Carlo looks, in Deco and in the wooden boards the colour is your role, not the site's colour, so it will not match the browser.

Other board choices
A different board each match, below the Board look cards, gives every match its own board from the ones you tick. While it is on, the cards turn into tick boxes and at least one stays ticked. A match keeps its board every time you open it, so returning to a match brings back the same board. Turning it off brings back the board you chose.

Dice and Score are separate choices: one die for each move or two dice as on the site, and points away from winning or points won as on the site. Each player card shows the whole score with that player's number first, for example 5-away 3-away, or 2-4/7 with the match length when you choose points won.

Waiting for DailyGammon picks what spins while the app waits for the site, in place of the buttons while a move is on its way and in the middle of a screen that is still loading. The choices are an arc, an ouroboros, a rolling doubling cube, a snake sliding along an infinity loop or an hourglass, all in the board's colours, and two golden laurel wreaths: one grows leaf by leaf and the other stays still while a gleam runs along it. A different one each time picks one of the seven at random for every wait, never the same twice in a row. Art deco and clockwork draws the same shape in black enamel and gold with small gears, in colours of its own. The wreaths are gold with or without it, and a darker bronze in light mode.

Theme
Theme at the top of This device switches several of these at once. Deco turns the app black and gold, sets Board look to Deco and turns on Art deco and clockwork. Plain puts back what you had before.

Wood turns the app honey maple in light mode and dark walnut in dark mode, with serif headings. It keeps the wooden board you have chosen, or sets Board look to Walnut if your board is not wooden, and the waiting shape takes the board's colours. The sounds go with Game sounds below the theme cards and work in every theme. They are off until you turn them on. The dice knock on wood when they land, a checker knocks when it moves and the doubling cube knocks when you double, take or beaver. The sounds keep quiet when the device is on silent or vibrate and while TalkBack is on, so they never cover its speech. The sounds were made for this app and carry no licence.

Deco follows the device's light or dark mode as Plain does: in light mode the app is ivory and brass, and the Deco board has ivory felt. In light mode the board screen around the board is light too, ivory in Deco and warm white in Plain, whatever board is on it, and the other boards keep their own colours. A Deco board chosen under Plain stays dark. In Deco the doubling cube is black enamel with a gold edge and gold numbers.

Deco headings use the Poiret One typeface by The Poiret One Project Authors, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

Cube and icon
When nobody has doubled yet, the doubling cube shows a robot instead of a 1. A physical cube has no face for 1, so this app puts its own mark there, and the value returns as soon as someone doubles. Each value has a colour of its own on the cube, from cream for 2 to white for 64, so the cube reads at a glance.

The app's launcher icon is the same cube with the robot on top. When the app opens on Android 12 or later, the cube is thrown like a die and settles with the robot on top, as on the icon. The Android robot is reproduced or modified from work created and shared by Google and used according to terms described in the Creative Commons 3.0 Attribution License.
Why do I have to press Take an item?

DailyGammon shows each message once and keeps no copy of it, so this app never fetches messages on its own: no background checking, no timer, no notifications.

On the Inbox tab, press Take an item to take one item from DailyGammon's queue. Each message is saved on this device before it appears on screen.

The explanation above the button is shown in full the first time and folded away after that. Tap Why? to read it again.
What else comes out of the queue besides messages?

An announcement from DailyGammon is shown but not saved.

A game board is not a message, so nothing is saved and nothing is lost: the match is in your match list. A board at the front of the queue also means the messages are read, so the notice on the list is cleared without a refresh.

An invitation to a match stays in the queue until you answer it here, with a comment if you like. Accepting starts the match on DailyGammon at once.

If the queue turns out to be empty, DailyGammon answers with your match list. Nothing is used up, and the Take an item button goes away until the list shows the notice again.
How do I reply, and what are the phrase buttons?

Tap a received message in the archive to open a reply box under it, and tap again to close it. Replies go to the sender, because DailyGammon addresses them to the player, not to the message.

Your replies are saved to the archive too, and a message you sent shows the name it went to after your own.

The phrase buttons under the box paste a saved phrase, and you can save your own text as a phrase or edit the list. Quote the message above in your reply adds the message you are answering.

When a match is over, its last page has Reply to under your opponent's score. It opens the same kind of box with the match name already quoted, and sends a quick message, the same kind a player's profile sends with Send. Once the message is sent the box closes and the note under the button says so.

DailyGammon itself does not offer this button. The idea comes from the DGText2Area browser extension.
How do I filter, export, back up or import the archive?

The Inbox opens on a list of the players you have messages with, one row each, the latest conversation first. A row shows how many messages there are, the day of the latest and its first line.

The count takes a colour by how the conversation ranks among yours by number of messages, from grey through green, blue and purple to orange, like item rarity in a role-playing game. A player's name takes the same colours by rating when the app has seen it, and stays plain otherwise. With Colour names by rating, tournaments by rounds and the Inbox count by size off in Settings, the count is plain and each name keeps a colour of its own instead.

Conversations marked New are highlighted, and when none is, the latest one is. A message fetched with Take an item moves its player to the top marked New, with the whole message and Reply, so you can answer it right there. The reply field is already open under a fresh message.

Tapping a row opens that conversation, and Back or All players returns to the list. The conversation you had open is kept on this device.

In a conversation, messages are listed under the day they arrived, newest first, each in its own bubble: what the other player sent on the left, what you sent on the right. A reply sits under the message it answers and shows its own day when that differs. Match after a name means the message came with a match, and tapping it opens the match. Quick means a quick message.

Export writes the whole archive to a file you choose. Back up chooses a file that the app rewrites with the current archive once a day, whenever the Inbox is open, and Save now writes it at once. The file holds your messages, reminders and phrases.

Import reads such a file and adds what this device does not have yet. Nothing already here is changed or removed, so an old file cannot overwrite newer messages. A message in Recently deleted is still on this device, so Import does not bring it back; use Restore instead.

Delete at the top of an open conversation moves the whole conversation to Recently deleted after you confirm. To delete one message, tap ⋮ in the corner of its bubble and choose Delete message; Copy text in the same menu copies the message. Right after a delete, Undo at the bottom of the screen brings it back.

Recently deleted is at the end of the player list, with each delete on its own row and Restore to bring it back. Deleted messages are left out of the list, the export and the backup file, and are removed for good 30 days after you deleted them. DailyGammon does not keep messages, so after that they come back only with Import from a file that still has them.
Why does it matter where I read my messages?

Your message archive is stored on the device where you take the messages, and nowhere else.
DailyGammon shows each message once, so a message read in a browser or in another app is gone from the site before this app can see it. It will never appear in the archive.
If you play on two devices with this app, each keeps its own archive, and Import merges them as the answer on moving your archive explains.
Playing your moves in a browser or in another app loses nothing, because moves stay on the site.
How do I move my archive to a new device, or merge two devices?

Export or Back up on the Inbox tab writes the archive to a file, and the app does not copy it anywhere by itself. The file is plain text you can read and keep.

Move the file to the new device and press Import on its Inbox tab. Messages, reminders and phrases come in, and anything the new device already has is left as it is.

Two devices you both play on are merged the same way: Import the file from each one on the other, in either order, as often as you like.

Marked positions are not in the file yet. Your choices under Settings move separately, with Save to file and Open file on the This device page.
What happens when I press Join or Sign Up?

The Lounge shows matches waiting for opponents and tournaments open for sign-up, read from the site. It has four sections, each behind a heading: Players, Tournament Hall, Matches waiting for opponents and Tournament sign-up.

Tapping a heading folds or unfolds its section: + means folded and − means shown. The app remembers the folds on this device.

Tournament Hall carries the number of rows in brackets, kept from the last time it was opened, so the number is there without fetching the page again. A question mark means the section has not been opened yet. Players carries no number, because the site gives no total.

Opening Players or Tournament Hall reads that page once. Refresh reads the lounge and any open section again.

Join and Sign Up ask you to confirm first, because a joined match starts at once and cannot be taken back. After you confirm Join, the app reads the lounge again and sends nothing if the match is no longer in the same place, because the site reuses the join link for a different match once the first is gone.

Cancel Signup is there for a tournament you signed up for.
Can I edit a forum post afterwards?

No. The Forum shows the site's threads and their posts. New starts a thread and Add a Comment answers in one.

Posts go to the public forum under your name and cannot be edited or deleted afterwards, so the app asks you to confirm before it sends.

Links inside a post open: a web address opens your browser, a DailyGammon page opens in the app.

Hide on a thread row hides that thread from the list on both General and Politics. The site keeps the choice, so it holds in a browser too.

Show Hidden Threads at the bottom of the list shows them again among the others, without a Hide button, and Hide Hidden Threads goes back. The site's thread list offers no Unhide, so the app has none either. A hidden thread stays readable from Show Hidden Threads.
Which settings stay on this device?

Settings has two parts, switched at the top, and Settings opens on This device.

This device
This device holds choices that live only on this device. They are kept as soon as you change them and are never sent to DailyGammon.

Theme comes first, with Game sounds below the cards, and below it four groups fold under their headings. They are all open until you close one, and the app remembers which are closed.

Board holds Board look and A different board each match, Dice, Score and Handedness, Right hand or Left hand.

Playing holds Place forced checkers for me and Bear off greedily for me, then Show arrows for my move and Show arrows for the opponent's move, then Show which point I'm pressing, then Submit the move by tapping the dice and Swap the dice by tapping them. Last comes Confirm Beaver for money games, which starts from Confirmation on offering doubles in your DailyGammon settings until you change it.

Lists and screens starts with Pictures below the lists, which shows pictures from a folder you choose on this device in the room left below the lists. Colour names by rating, tournaments by rounds and the Inbox count by size is on unless you turn it off. Waiting for DailyGammon comes last, with Art deco and clockwork.

Screen and lock holds Keep lists and messages upright and Turn the board with the device, then Hide the status and navigation bars, which is off unless you turn it on. Ask for fingerprint or PIN when the app starts is off unless you turn it on. On a phone every screen turns upright while you type, whatever these switches say, so the field and its button stay above the keyboard. The sign-in screen is always upright. On a tablet with Android 16 or later, Android itself turns every screen with the device, so the two orientation switches have no effect there.

Below the groups, Save to file writes these choices, the match list order and the Inbox player filter to a file as one line of text, wherever you choose, Google Drive included. On another device, Open file shows which of them would change and uses them only when you confirm. Your sign-in, app lock, messages, quick messages and pictures folder are not in the text.

The choice cards
Theme, Board look, Dice, Score and Waiting for DailyGammon show each choice as a card with a picture of the same game position, drawn the way that choice draws it. The waiting cards spin as they would on the board.

The two Handedness cards are mirror images of each other, whatever the site is set to. Left hand shows the home board on the left, next to the hand that moves the checkers. The board itself turns that way only with Home boards on left side under DailyGammon.

Tapping the picture on a card shows it large, where Use this picks it. Tapping the name below the picture picks it straight away.

DailyGammon
DailyGammon is the site's own settings form for your account, read from the site when you open it. Update Preferences and the count of changes stay at the bottom of the screen while the form scrolls.

Nothing is sent until you press Update Preferences. While the form differs from what was read, the button gets a purple frame that pulses a few times and then stays, like the cube reminder on the board.

Board Scheme is shown as cards with the same game position, following what is ticked in the form before it is sent. Mini can't be chosen here because this app can't show that board. If it is already set on the site, it stays set.

Background Color changes only the page colour on the website, so it is a plain list: this app keeps its own background. The large picture and its Use this only fill in the form.

DailyGammon saves that form as a whole, so every field is sent even if you change one. The app reads the page back, and only a matching read-back counts as saved.

Change Password and Public Profile are not in the app: the row above the form opens the site's settings page in your browser.
What does this app never do?

Nothing goes to DailyGammon without a press from you: no move, no message, no join, no post.

The app does nothing in the background: no checking, no timer, no notifications.

It reads only the pages you open, and it keeps only what those pages showed you, on this device and nowhere else.
Your matches and message history are stored on this device only.
